title: Technical Interview Sprint
summary: You're 10 minutes into a technical interview. The interviewer just asked you to walk through how you'd approach a problem you've never seen before — not solve it perfectly, just show your thinking.

title: Behavioral Interview (STAR Method)
summary: An interviewer asks: 'Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision at work or school. What did you do?' You have about 90 seconds to answer well.

title: 60-Second Elevator Pitch Challenge
summary: A recruiter you've been hoping to meet just asked, 'So, tell me about yourself.' You have about 60 seconds before they need to move to the next person in line.

title: Difficult Feedback Conversation
summary: A team member has missed the same deadline twice in three weeks, and you have a 1-on-1 with them in 15 minutes. You need to raise it directly without being harsh.

title: Budget Cut Decision Sprint
summary: Your department's budget just got cut by 15% for next quarter. You have four ongoing initiatives and need to decide what to cut, reduce, or protect — before the finance meeting in 20 minutes.

title: Safety Walk Simulation
summary: You're doing a routine safety walk on an active site. You have about 10 minutes to spot hazards before reporting back to the site manager.

title: Scope Creep Conversation
summary: A client asks, mid-call, 'Can you also just quickly add X?' — a request that's outside the original agreed scope and would take real time, but they're framing it as small.

title: Code Review Roleplay
summary: You're reviewing a colleague's code and found a real bug — a function that will fail under certain inputs. You need to leave a comment on it.

title: Root Cause 5-Whys Sprint
summary: A website went down for 20 minutes. The immediate cause was a server running out of memory. Your team lead wants the real root cause before everyone moves on, not just 'the server ran out of memory.'

title: Delegation Decision Sprint
summary: You have a task that needs doing this week: preparing a client-facing summary report. You could do it yourself (30 min, guaranteed quality) or delegate it to a capable but newer team member (they'd need 90 min and some guidance, but it's a good growth opportunity for them).

title: Bid/No-Bid Decision Sprint
summary: A tender opportunity just landed — a project that fits your company's expertise well, but the client has a reputation for slow payment and the tender preparation itself will cost real time and money with no guarantee of winning.

title: AI Prompt Challenge
summary: You need an AI assistant to help draft a professional email to a client about a project delay. Your first prompt attempt got a generic, unhelpful response. You have one more try to get something usable.
